title: My Wife’s Family Used Our Pool for Years—Then They Destroyed It While We Were on Vacation

blocks.text: For years, I tried to keep the peace with my wife’s family.
That decision eventually cost me $27,640.
After Sarah and I bought our house, her family discovered that we had something everyone seemed to love—a large backyard pool.
At first, Kevin, Sarah’s younger brother, would ask before coming over.
One Saturday afternoon, I came home and found Kevin, his wife, and their three kids swimming in our pool.
“They wanted to cool off,” she said. “It’s not a big deal.”
Soon, they had practically turned our backyard into their private resort.
They even started keeping pool toys in our storage shed.
Whenever I mentioned it, Sarah told me not to make things awkward.
A few weeks before our Yosemite trip, Kevin mentioned that his family was planning a camping weekend.
I happened to own a large, expensive tent that could comfortably sleep six people.
“Hey, Kevin. Could I borrow one of your smaller tents for a night? I need it for our trip.”
“Man, you have a pool in your backyard and you’re worried about borrowing a tent?”
The same family that had been using my pool whenever they wanted was laughing because I asked to borrow something.
That was the moment something inside me changed.
Seven days later, Sarah and I returned from Yosemite.
Our luggage was still sitting in the hallway when I stepped outside to check the pool.
Nearly 28,000 gallons of water were gone.
The liner had pulled away from the walls.
The automatic vacuum was broken beside the main drain.
Several cedar planters had been knocked over.
Potting soil was scattered across the patio.
Snack wrappers were stuffed underneath the patio table.
And sitting in the middle of that table was a heavy landscaping rock.
I recognized the handwriting immediately.
“Hope you enjoyed your little vacation.”
He spent almost two hours inspecting the damage.
Then I looked at the photographs on my phone.
The technician pointed toward the pool equipment.
He showed me the damaged drain assembly.
“Someone appears to have deliberately interfered with the system.”
I asked him whether the damage could have happened accidentally.
Before she could even ask what happened, he said:
Then Kevin said, “Because we were there.”
Kevin admitted that his family had used the pool while we were gone.
But he insisted that the damage wasn’t their fault.
“Something must have gone wrong with the filter,” he said.
“You have until tomorrow morning to explain exactly what happened.”
The next morning, I changed the locks on the backyard gate.
Then I disabled the pool’s remote access.
Then I did something else Sarah had never expected.
I stopped paying the bills I had been covering for her family.
For years, I’d quietly helped Kevin with several expenses.
A portion of his family’s internet bill.
I had done it because Sarah kept telling me they were struggling.
Then he said something I never expected.
And that’s when the real story finally came out.
Kevin told me that when his family arrived that night, someone was already inside our backyard.
Kevin said they assumed he was someone I had hired.
A few hours later, they heard a loud mechanical noise.
His answer was almost impossible to believe.
But the final line—the one written in red ink—looked different.
And this time, I noticed something I’d completely missed.
There was a small security-camera symbol drawn beneath the message.
The backyard camera had been disconnected.
But our front-door camera was still working.
I pulled up the footage from the night we were gone.
At 2:13 a.m., a dark SUV stopped outside our house.
